comments.why: Teaches benchmarking on Linux and how C++ becomes machine code.
comments.text: Here's a few: - "Tuning C++: Benchmarks, and CPUs, and Compilers! Oh My!" [VIDEO] - "Understanding Compiler Optimization" [LINK] - "Optimizing the Emergent Structures of C++" [LINK] - "Efficiency with Algorithms" [LINK] The first one is really good if you've never benchmarked anything in a Linux environment. Or if you otherwise want to learn how to investigate how C++ gets turned into machine code.

comments.why: Talk on benchmarking pitfalls and stopping compilers optimizing benchmark code away
comments.text: > Anecdote: Optimum C blew away all the other C compilers on a magazine benchmark article because it figured out that the benchmark code did nothing and deleted it. I remember this problem being discussed in a CPPCon talk a few years ago, and some ways to "trick" the (modern) compilers into not optimising away the benchmark code - I think it was Chandler Carruth's "Tuning C++" talk: [VIDEO]
